author: mvafin
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - tbb12.dll locked (Access denied) on Windows self-hosted runner
signature: remove item cannot remove item access to the path is denied unauthorizedaccessexception|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Expand-Archive cannot overwrite tbb12.dll - Access denied

key_errors: Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll: Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force over the previous install directory on a Windows self-hosted runner. tbb12.dll from the prior job/run is still memory-mapped or locked by another process (e.g. a lingering test process or antivirus scan) when the next job starts, so the archive module's attempt to overwrite/remove the existing DLL fails with UnauthorizedAccessException. This is the 9th recorded occurrence of the same signature since 2026-11-09, always on the same step across various self-hosted Windows GPU runners, consistent with a runner-level file-lock/cleanup race rather than a code defect in this PR.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires a Windows self-hosted runner where the install directory from a previous job run still has a locked tbb12.dll; cannot be reproduced in a clean environment. Can be approximated by: 1) load tbb12.dll into a running process; 2) attempt `Expand-Archive -Force` to overwrite the install directory containing that DLL.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'GPU unit tests' job (transient lock typically clears) - requested automatically via remediate_transient_failure
Add a retry-with-backoff wrapper around the Expand-Archive/Remove-Item extraction step for Windows jobs to absorb transient file locks

Investigate whether a lingering process (test runner, antivirus, Windows Search indexer) from the prior job on these self-hosted runners is holding a handle to tbb12.dll after job completion, and add an explicit cleanup/handle-release step at job end
Consider isolating the install directory per-job (unique path) instead of reusing a shared extraction directory across jobs on the same runner
prevention_strategies: Add automated retry logic (3 attempts with short backoff) around the archive extraction step on Windows self-hosted runners. Ensure runner job cleanup steps explicitly close/release file handles (e.g., via Restart-Service or explicit process termination) before marking a job complete, so the next job's extraction does not race a still-held lock on shared binaries like tbb12.dll.
historical_context: This exact signature has now occurred 9 times since 2026-11-09T19:06:46Z, with 5 occurrences in the last 12 hours (escalation threshold reached), affecting PRs #39617, #37406, #39577, #39668, #39034, #39444 and now #39653.
